newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy sees no renegotiation of EU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy sees no renegotiation of EU budget pact.

text.p: No one in the European Union is considering renegotiating the "stability pact" meant to limit budget deficits after the launch of monetary union, European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Monday.

French Socialist party officials have said they would seek new discussions on the pact if the left wins power in France's parliamentary election. First round results on Sunday suggested the combined left could win in the second round next Sunday.
"No one is considering renegotiating the stability and growth pact," he told a news conference during a meeting of ministers of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
He said all conditions necessary for the launch of the single currency were in place.
"The euro will be launched on January 1, 1999. We are now on the home straight. It is up to member states to continue their (economic) convergence efforts to qualify (to join)," he said.
